title: Surjectivity conjecture for the group enumeration function
statement:
Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups of order $n$. **Surjectivity conjecture.** For every positive integer $m$, there exists an integer $n$ such that

$$
f(n)=m.
$$

This conjecture asks whether every positive integer occurs as the number of groups of some order. The surrounding discussion concerns known formulas and bounds for $f(n)$, but gives no resolution of this surjectivity question.
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1911.11172](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11172).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25230

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
source_name: Shihan Kanungo, “Classifying Groups of Certain Orders”, arXiv:2606.25230 (2026).
